question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Existentialism has a reputation for being angst-ridden and gloomy mostly because of its emphasis on pondering the meaningless of existence.
option_1: on pondering the meaningless of existence
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. on pondering the meaningless of existence.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The preposition "of" in "the ______ of existence" must be followed by a noun. "Meaningless" is an adjective; the noun form required here is "meaninglessness".

◦ Correct: Existentialism has a reputation for being angst-ridden and gloomy mostly because of its emphasis on pondering the meaninglessness of existence.

• The structure "the + NOUN + of + NOUN" (the meaninglessness of existence, the beauty of nature, the vastness of space) demands an abstract noun after "the".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "mostly because of its emphasis" is correct — "because of" is a compound preposition followed by the noun "emphasis".

• Option 3 "Existentialism has a reputation" is correct — singular subject with singular verb "has".

• Option 4 "for being angst-ridden and gloomy" is correct — the preposition "for" is correctly followed by the gerund "being", and the two adjectives are parallel.

NOTE

• Adjective → Abstract noun conversions frequently tested in SSC exams: meaningless → meaninglessness, happy → happiness, wise → wisdom, brave → bravery, strong → strength, poor → poverty, able → ability.

• Existentialism (अस्तित्ववाद) is a philosophy associated with Sartre, Camus and Kierkegaard that stresses individual freedom and the absence of inherent meaning in life.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

To preparing the vine for plant, it should be cut back to 2 ft.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. prepare the vine for planting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "To" here is the sign of the infinitive (to + V1), so it must be followed by the base form of the verb — "to prepare", not "to preparing / to prepares / to prepared".

• The preposition "for" must be followed by a noun or gerund, hence "for planting" (not "for plant").

◦ Correct: To prepare the vine for planting, it should be cut back to 2 ft.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "prepares in vine in plant" — wrong verb form after "to" and wrong prepositions.

• Option 2 "prepare a vine in planting" — the article and the preposition "in" are both wrong; the specific vine already referred to requires "the".

• Option 3 "prepared the vine of plant" — past form after "to" is incorrect.

NOTE

• Rule: to + V1 (infinitive) — to go, to prepare, to write.

• Rule: preposition + V-ing (gerund) — for planting, before leaving, after eating, in spite of trying.

• Do not confuse the infinitive "to" with the preposition "to" (look forward to meeting, be used to working).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.

The student provided her English teacher a short and _________(incoherent) account of her journey to Shimla with her parents.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. lucid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Incoherent" means unclear, confused, not logically connected; impossible to understand. (असंगत / अस्पष्ट)

• Its antonym is "lucid", which means clear, easily understood, expressed clearly. (स्पष्ट)

◦ Correct: The student provided her English teacher a short and lucid account of her journey to Shimla with her parents.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 humble means modest, not proud (विनम्र) — it is not the opposite of "incoherent".

• Option 3 rough means uneven, coarse, approximate (खुरदरा) — no antonym relation.

• Option 4 genuine means real, authentic (वास्तविक) — the opposite of "fake", not of "incoherent".

NOTE

• Synonyms of incoherent: rambling, disjointed, confused, muddled, unintelligible, garbled.

• Synonyms of lucid: clear, intelligible, coherent, comprehensible, transparent, articulate.

• Related SSC word: lucidity (noun) = clarity of expression.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I want to / give you / an information about / the missing necklace.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. an information about.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Information" is an uncountable (non-count) noun. Uncountable nouns can never take the article "a/an" and have no plural form.

◦ Correct: I want to give you information about / a piece of information about / some information about the missing necklace.

• The article "an" must therefore be removed, or the quantifier "a piece of" must be used.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Segment "I want to" is correct (want + to-infinitive).

• Segment "give you" is correct (the base form after "to").

• Segment "the missing necklace" is correct (definite article with a specific noun).

NOTE

• Common uncountable nouns in SSC exams: information, advice, furniture, luggage, baggage, equipment, machinery, scenery, poetry, stationery, news, work, bread, money, traffic, evidence.

• They take a singular verb and are quantified with "a piece of / an item of / some / much / a little": a piece of advice, two items of furniture, much information.

question:
Identify the most appropriate meaning of the given word.

Ancient
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Antique.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ancient" means belonging to the very distant past; very old. (प्राचीन)

• "Antique" means belonging to an earlier period; old and often valuable because of its age. (पुरातन / प्राचीन वस्तु) It is the closest in meaning to "ancient".

◦ Example: The museum displays ancient/antique coins from the Mauryan period.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 Unworn means never worn or used — this refers to condition, not age.

• Option 3 Contemporary means belonging to the present time; modern (समकालीन) — an antonym of ancient.

• Option 4 Recent means having happened a short time ago (हाल का) — also an antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of ancient: old, aged, archaic, primeval, antediluvian, age-old, bygone, olden.

• Antonyms of ancient: modern, recent, contemporary, current, new, present-day.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

They are sell their company’s products to people.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. are selling their company’s.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The auxiliary "are" belongs to the present continuous tense, whose structure is "is/am/are + V-ing". So "are sell" is wrong; it must be "are selling".

• The subject "They" is plural, so the possessive adjective must be "their", and the possessive noun "company’s" correctly shows ownership of the products.

◦ Correct: They are selling their company’s products to people.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "are sell the company" — wrong verb form and the possessive is lost.

• Option 3 "was sell the company’s" — "was" does not agree with the plural subject "They", and "sell" is the wrong form.

• Option 4 "is selling they company’s" — "is" does not agree with "They", and "they" cannot be used as a possessive adjective (it must be "their").

NOTE

• Present continuous: is/am/are + V1 + ing — used for actions happening now or around now.

• Possessive adjectives: my, our, your, his, her, its, their. Possessive pronouns: mine, ours, yours, his, hers, theirs.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

Mary is a ball of fire and is always engaged in something creative.
option_3: To be good and beneficial for someone
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. An active and energetic person.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a ball of fire" refers to an extremely energetic, dynamic and enthusiastic person who is always full of activity. (अत्यंत ऊर्जावान व्यक्ति)

• The second half of the sentence — "is always engaged in something creative" — confirms this sense.

◦ Example: The new intern is a ball of fire; she finishes three assignments before lunch.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "A dull and insipid person" is the exact opposite of the idiom's meaning.

• Option 3 "To be good and beneficial for someone" corresponds to idioms like "do someone a world of good".

• Option 4 "A talkative person" corresponds to "a chatterbox" or "talk nineteen to the dozen".

NOTE

• Related idioms of energy/enthusiasm: "full of beans", "live wire", "go-getter", "bundle of energy", "raring to go".

• Related idioms of dullness: "as dull as ditchwater", "a wet blanket", "a stick-in-the-mud".

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

By living in a rural area with access to the city, she gets _______________.
option_2: to keep an ear to the ground
option_4: in for a penny in for a pound
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. the best of both worlds.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "the best of both worlds" means to enjoy the advantages of two different situations at the same time. (दोनों स्थितियों के लाभ एक साथ पाना)

• Living in a rural area (peace, greenery, low cost) while still having access to the city (jobs, facilities) is exactly the enjoyment of two advantages at once.

◦ Correct: By living in a rural area with access to the city, she gets the best of both worlds.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "keep an ear to the ground" = to stay well informed about what is happening (सतर्क रहना).

• Option 3 "on cloud nine" = extremely happy or elated (अत्यंत प्रसन्न).

• Option 4 "in for a penny, in for a pound" = once you begin something, you should complete it however much effort it takes.

NOTE

• Note the grammar: "gets the best of both worlds" fits the verb "gets"; option 2 begins with the infinitive "to keep" and is grammatically unsuitable after "gets" here.

• Similar idiom: "have your cake and eat it too" — to enjoy two incompatible benefits (used with a slightly negative sense).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The cats food bowl was empty, so he meowed incessantly until his owner finally filled it with fresh kibble.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The cat’s.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The bowl belongs to the cat, so the possessive case is required. For a singular noun the possessive is formed by adding apostrophe + s — "the cat’s food bowl".

• The pronouns later in the sentence — "he meowed" and "his owner" — are singular, proving that only one cat is meant.

◦ Correct: The cat’s food bowl was empty, so he meowed incessantly until his owner finally filled it with fresh kibble.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "The cats’" is the plural possessive (more than one cat) and clashes with "he/his".

• Option 3 "A cats’" mixes the singular article "a" with a plural possessive — grammatically impossible.

• Option 2 "A cat’s" is grammatically formed correctly but the definite article "the" is needed because a specific cat is being talked about (and referred back to as "he").

NOTE

• Possessive rules: singular noun → ’s (boy’s); regular plural ending in -s → ’ only (boys’); irregular plural → ’s (children’s, men’s, women’s).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Get your act together
option_4: Get organised and do things better
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Get organised and do things better.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "get your act together" means to organise yourself and start behaving or performing in a more effective, disciplined way. (स्वयं को व्यवस्थित करना और बेहतर काम करना)

◦ Example: If you want to clear the SSC exam, you must get your act together and follow a strict timetable.

• It is generally used as advice or a mild rebuke to someone whose work or life is disorganised.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "To have patience" corresponds to "hold your horses" or "bide your time".

• Option 2 "To stay together" corresponds to "stick together".

• Option 3 "To act in a play" is the literal meaning of "act" and is a trap; idioms are never interpreted literally.

NOTE

• Similar idioms: "pull yourself together" (regain composure), "shape up" (improve behaviour), "get one’s house in order" (put one’s affairs in order).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Unpleasant
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Nasty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Nasty" means very unpleasant, disagreeable, offensive or objectionable. (अप्रिय / गंदा)

◦ Example: There was a nasty smell coming from the drain.

• Among the four options, only "nasty" carries the sense of "unpleasant".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Nebulous = vague, hazy, unclear in form or outline (अस्पष्ट).

• Option 2 Natal = relating to the place or time of one’s birth (जन्म संबंधी); e.g. natal city, pre-natal care.

• Option 3 Negligible = so small or unimportant as to be not worth considering (नगण्य).

NOTE

• Synonyms of nasty: unpleasant, disgusting, foul, obnoxious, repugnant, vile, horrid.

• Antonyms of nasty: pleasant, agreeable, delightful, nice, kind.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.

(A) The mother exclaimed / (B) when she saw her son / (C) stumble on the race track, / (D) “Look, he fells!”
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. D.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Part (D) reads "Look, he fells!" — the verb "fells" is wrong. "Fell" (fells, felling, felled) is a transitive verb meaning to cut down a tree or to knock someone down.

• The intended verb is "fall", and with the third-person singular subject "he" it becomes "falls".

◦ Correct: (D) "Look, he falls!"

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Part (A) "The mother exclaimed" is correct.

• Part (B) "when she saw her son" is correct.

• Part (C) "stumble on the race track" is correct — after the verb of perception "saw", the bare infinitive ("stumble") is used: saw him stumble / saw him stumbling.

NOTE

• fall (fall – fell – fallen) = to drop down, intransitive.

• fell (fell – felled – felled) = to cut down / knock down, transitive: They felled the old banyan tree.

• Verbs of perception (see, hear, watch, notice, feel) take bare infinitive (V1) or V-ing, never "to + V1".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to rectify it, select ‘no rectification needed’.

The conductor said that it was the worse quake he ever knew.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. worst.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The definite article "the" immediately before the adjective, together with the clause "he ever knew", signals the superlative degree. The superlative of "bad" is "worst".

• Degrees of comparison: bad – worse – worst. "Worse" is the comparative and is used with "than", which is absent here.

◦ Correct: The conductor said that it was the worst quake he ever knew.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "more bad" is a double comparative and is always incorrect.

• Option 2 "bad" (positive degree) cannot follow "the ... he ever knew" structure.

• Option 3 "no rectification needed" is wrong because the sentence as given contains a clear degree error.

NOTE

• The pattern "the + superlative + (that) ... ever + V2" is standard: the best film I ever saw, the worst storm we ever faced.

• Irregular degrees: good – better – best; bad – worse – worst; little – less – least; much/many – more – most; far – farther/further – farthest/furthest.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence.

After having invested so much time and energy into the project, we are now back to square one.
option_4: Having to start all over again
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Having to start all over again.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "back to square one" means to return to the very beginning because the previous effort has failed; to have to start again from scratch. (फिर से शुरुआत करनी पड़ना)

• The contrast marker "After having invested so much time and energy ... we are now" shows that all that effort has come to nothing.

◦ Example: The client rejected the design, so the team was back to square one.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Not ready for the consequence" is unrelated to the idiom.

• Option 2 "In the same city" is a literal-sounding distractor with no idiomatic basis.

• Option 3 "Fighting with each other" corresponds to idioms like "at loggerheads" or "at each other’s throats".

NOTE

• The idiom is thought to come from board games (or early radio football commentary) where a player must return to the first square.

• Similar idioms: "start from scratch", "go back to the drawing board", "square one".

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Killing of one’s own father
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Patricide.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Patricide" is the killing of one’s own father (Latin pater = father + cide = killing). (पितृहत्या)

◦ Example: In Greek tragedy, Oedipus is guilty of patricide without knowing it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Matricide = killing of one’s own mother (मातृहत्या).

• Option 2 Filicide = killing of one’s own son or daughter.

• Option 4 Suicide = killing of oneself (आत्महत्या).

NOTE

• Important "-cide" words for SSC: homicide (a human being), fratricide (brother), sororicide (sister), uxoricide (wife), mariticide (husband), infanticide (infant), regicide (king), genocide (a race/community), germicide (germs), insecticide (insects), pesticide (pests), herbicide (plants/weeds), deicide (a god).

question:
The sentence given below has spelling errors. Select the sentence without spelling errors.

Though we read and hear a lot on green initiattive, we hardly tweak our routines to suite the larger picture.
option_1: Though we read and hear a lot on green initiatives, we hardly tweak our routines to suit the larger picture.
option_2: Throug we read and hear a lot on green initiatives, we hardly tweak our routines to suite the larger picture.
option_3: Though we read and hear a lot on green initiatives, we hardly tweek our routines to suite the larger picture.
option_4: Though we read and hear a lot on green iniciatives, we hardly tweak our routines to suite the larger picture.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Though we read and hear a lot on green initiatives, we hardly tweak our routines to suit the larger picture.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence has two spelling errors: "initiattive" → initiatives, and "suite" → suit.

• Only Option 1 corrects both errors and keeps every other word correctly spelt:

◦ Though (correct), initiatives (correct), tweak (correct), suit (correct).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 misspells "Though" as "Throug" and retains "suite".

• Option 3 misspells "tweak" as "tweek" and retains "suite".

• Option 4 misspells "initiatives" as "iniciatives" and retains "suite".

NOTE

• Suit (verb) = to be convenient or appropriate for (अनुकूल होना); suite (noun) = a set of rooms or a set of matching furniture / a musical composition.

• Tweak = to make small adjustments (हल्का बदलाव करना).

• Initiative = a new plan or process to achieve something (पहल); plural initiatives.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank.

The athlete’s injury was a ________(defeat) for the team’s chances of winning the championship.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. setback.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Defeat" here carries the sense of a reverse, a check to progress, something that hinders success. Its closest synonym in the given options is "setback" — a problem that delays or reverses progress. (झटका / बाधा)

◦ Correct: The athlete’s injury was a setback for the team’s chances of winning the championship.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 progression = a forward movement or advance — the opposite sense.

• Option 2 breakthrough = a sudden important discovery or success — again the opposite.

• Option 3 stress = mental or emotional strain (तनाव) — it does not mean "defeat".

NOTE

• Synonyms of setback: reverse, blow, hitch, obstacle, hindrance, impediment, misfortune, upset.

• Antonyms of setback: advance, boost, breakthrough, progress, gain.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Irresistable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word is incorrectly spelt. The correct spelling is "irresistible" — with the suffix "-ible", not "-able".

• "Irresistible" means too attractive or tempting to be resisted. (जिसका विरोध न किया जा सके)

◦ Correct: The aroma of freshly baked bread was irresistible.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Parallel is correctly spelt (one "r", two "l"s in the middle, one "l" at the end): PA-RA-LLEL.

• Option 2 Recommend is correctly spelt (one "c", two "m"s): RE-COM-MEND.

• Option 4 Tomorrow is correctly spelt (one "m", two "r"s): TO-MOR-ROW.

NOTE

• Words taking -ible: irresistible, responsible, possible, visible, terrible, edible, feasible, legible, plausible, compatible.

• Words taking -able: comfortable, reliable, valuable, admirable, remarkable, unbelievable.

question: Select the correctly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Millennium.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Millennium" — double "l" and double "n": MI-LLE-NNI-UM.

• It comes from Latin mille (= thousand) + annus (= year) and means a period of one thousand years. (सहस्राब्दी)

◦ Example: The millennium celebrations of the year 2000 were watched worldwide.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Milennium" has only one "l" — incorrect.

• Option 3 "Millenum" drops an "n" and an "i" — incorrect.

• Option 4 "Milenium" has single "l" and single "n" — incorrect.

NOTE

• Plural: millennia (or millenniums).

• Related time words: decade (10 years), score (20 years), century (100 years), millennium (1,000 years).

• Other Latin mille words: millipede, million, millimetre.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.

She proposed to write the life history of the famous poet.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. biography.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "biography" is an account of a person’s life written by someone else. Since she proposes to write the life history of the famous poet (a different person), the correct word is "biography". (जीवनी)

◦ Correct: She proposed to write the biography of the famous poet.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 novel = a long fictional prose narrative (उपन्यास) — not a life history.

• Option 3 mythology = a body of myths belonging to a culture (पुराण-कथा).

• Option 4 autobiography = the life history of a person written by that person himself/herself (आत्मकथा). It is the classic trap here: she is writing about someone else, so it cannot be an autobiography.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: biography (life written by another), autobiography (life written by oneself), memoir (an account of personal experiences), biographer (one who writes a biography), hagiography (life of a saint), obituary (notice of a death with a short biography).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Democracy is a form of government where the power lies ______(1) the people. It is based on the principles of equality, freedom and the rule of law. In a democratic society, ______(2) have the right to participate in the decision-making process, _________(3) directly or through elected representatives. Democracy also allows for the ________(4) of individual rights and liberties. While democracy is not without its challenges, such as the need to balance competing interests and the risk of ___________(5) movements, it remains one of the most widely embraced forms of government around the world.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. with.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed expression is "power lies with (someone)", meaning the authority is held by / rests with that person or body.

◦ Correct: Democracy is a form of government where the power lies with the people.

• "Lie with" is a standard collocation: the decision lies with the committee, the responsibility lies with the parents.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "lies towards" indicates direction/location (the village lies towards the north) — wrong sense here.

• Option 2 "lies on" indicates physical position (the book lies on the table).

• Option 3 "lies by" is not an accepted collocation for authority.

NOTE

• Democracy literally means "rule by the people" (Greek demos = people, kratos = rule); Abraham Lincoln defined it as "government of the people, by the people, for the people".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Democracy is a form of government where the power lies ______(1) the people. It is based on the principles of equality, freedom and the rule of law. In a democratic society, ______(2) have the right to participate in the decision-making process, _________(3) directly or through elected representatives. Democracy also allows for the ________(4) of individual rights and liberties. While democracy is not without its challenges, such as the need to balance competing interests and the risk of ___________(5) movements, it remains one of the most widely embraced forms of government around the world.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. citizens.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs the group that, in a democratic society, has "the right to participate in the decision-making process ... directly or through elected representatives". That group is the "citizens" — the legally recognised members of a state. (नागरिक)

◦ Correct: In a democratic society, citizens have the right to participate in the decision-making process ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "lawyers" is far too narrow a professional group.

• Option 2 "humans" is too broad — political rights in a state belong to its citizens, not to all human beings everywhere.

• Option 3 "politicians" contradicts the passage, which distinguishes participation "directly" from participation "through elected representatives".

NOTE

• The passage earlier says the power lies with the people; "citizens" is the precise term that continues that idea, so it also gives contextual cohesion.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Democracy is a form of government where the power lies ______(1) the people. It is based on the principles of equality, freedom and the rule of law. In a democratic society, ______(2) have the right to participate in the decision-making process, _________(3) directly or through elected representatives. Democracy also allows for the ________(4) of individual rights and liberties. While democracy is not without its challenges, such as the need to balance competing interests and the risk of ___________(5) movements, it remains one of the most widely embraced forms of government around the world.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. either.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is followed later by "or" — "________ directly or through elected representatives". The correlative conjunction that pairs with "or" is "either".

◦ Correct: ... participate in the decision-making process, either directly or through elected representatives.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "neither" pairs with "nor", not with "or".

• Option 2 "however" is a contrast connector and does not fit a two-choice structure.

• Option 4 "also" pairs with "not only ... but also" and cannot introduce a simple alternative.

NOTE

• Correlative conjunction pairs: either ... or, neither ... nor, not only ... but also, both ... and, whether ... or, no sooner ... than, scarcely ... when.

• The elements joined must be parallel — here both are adverbial phrases of manner ("directly" / "through elected representatives").

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Democracy is a form of government where the power lies ______(1) the people. It is based on the principles of equality, freedom and the rule of law. In a democratic society, ______(2) have the right to participate in the decision-making process, _________(3) directly or through elected representatives. Democracy also allows for the ________(4) of individual rights and liberties. While democracy is not without its challenges, such as the need to balance competing interests and the risk of ___________(5) movements, it remains one of the most widely embraced forms of government around the world.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. protection.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is positive about democracy — "Democracy also allows for the ________ of individual rights and liberties." A democracy safeguards rights, so the required noun is "protection". (संरक्षण)

◦ Correct: Democracy also allows for the protection of individual rights and liberties.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 delimitation = the act of fixing boundaries or limits (परिसीमन) — in India it refers to redrawing constituency boundaries; it does not fit "rights and liberties" positively.

• Option 3 diversion = turning something aside from its course; also an amusement (मोड़ना) — irrelevant.

• Option 4 proscription = the act of forbidding or banning something (प्रतिबंध) — the exact opposite of what a democracy does with rights.

NOTE

• The linker "also" adds one more merit of democracy to the merits already listed (equality, freedom, rule of law, participation), so the blank must carry a positive meaning.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Democracy is a form of government where the power lies ______(1) the people. It is based on the principles of equality, freedom and the rule of law. In a democratic society, ______(2) have the right to participate in the decision-making process, _________(3) directly or through elected representatives. Democracy also allows for the ________(4) of individual rights and liberties. While democracy is not without its challenges, such as the need to balance competing interests and the risk of ___________(5) movements, it remains one of the most widely embraced forms of government around the world.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. populist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank comes after "the risk of ______ movements", listed among the challenges of democracy. The movements most commonly identified as a risk to democratic systems are "populist" movements — those that claim to speak for ordinary people against the elite, often by simplistic or emotive appeals. (लोकलुभावन)

◦ Correct: ... the risk of populist movements, it remains one of the most widely embraced forms of government ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 marginal = small, insignificant, on the edge — a marginal movement would hardly be a "risk".

• Option 2 elitist = favouring a select privileged group; the standard collocation with "movements" as a democratic risk is "populist", and "elitist movements" is not idiomatic here.

• Option 4 negligible = too small to be worth considering — it directly contradicts the word "risk".

NOTE

• Populism (लोकलुभावनवाद) = a political approach that appeals to ordinary people who feel their concerns are disregarded by established elite groups.

• Note the word family: populist (adj./noun), populism (noun), popular, populace, populous.

question: Who among the following is primarily regarded as a maestro of Hindustani classical music?

question: What is ‘Mahawat’ in India?
option_1: Cold waves during the winter season
option_2: Cloud burst during the monsoon season
option_3: Cyclonic rainfall during the winter season
option_4: Hot and dry winds during the summer season
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Cyclonic rainfall during the winter season.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mahawat" (महावट) is the local name in North India for the light winter rainfall brought by Western Disturbances — extra-tropical cyclonic storms that originate over the Mediterranean Sea and travel eastwards across Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan into North-West India.

• Though small in amount, this winter rain is extremely important for the rabi crops, especially wheat, and is therefore called "golden drops" by farmers.

• It occurs mainly in December–February over Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Rajasthan, western Uttar Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 refers to cold waves (sheet lahar), a temperature phenomenon, not rainfall.

• Option 2 cloud burst is sudden very heavy rainfall (>100 mm/hour) during the monsoon, common in the Himalayas.

• Option 4 hot and dry winds during summer in North India are called "Loo".

NOTE

• Other local Indian weather/wind names: Loo (hot summer wind, N India), Kaal Baisakhi (pre-monsoon thunderstorms in West Bengal/Assam), Norwesters, Mango Showers (Kerala/Karnataka, help mango ripening), Blossom Showers (coffee flowering in Kerala), Cherry Blossom / Coffee Blossom showers, Bardoli Chheerha (Assam).

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India deals with the organization of village panchayat?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Article 40.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 40 of the Constitution of India, one of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP, Part IV), states that the State shall take steps to organise village panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government. (ग्राम पंचायतों का संगठन)

• It is a Gandhian principle and formed the constitutional basis for the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, which gave Panchayati Raj Institutions constitutional status (Part IX, Articles 243 to 243-O, Eleventh Schedule with 29 subjects).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Article 36 — Definition of "the State" for Part IV.

• Article 38 — State to secure a social order for the promotion of welfare of the people.

• Article 45 — Provision for early childhood care and education to children below six years of age (amended by the 86th Amendment, 2002).

• Article 39 — Certain principles of policy: adequate means of livelihood, equal pay for equal work, distribution of material resources.

• Article 44 — Uniform Civil Code; Article 48A — protection of environment; Article 50 — separation of judiciary from executive.

NOTE

• Panchayati Raj was first inaugurated at Nagaur, Rajasthan on 2 October 1959 by Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru, on the recommendation of the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957).

• Later committees: Ashok Mehta Committee (1977), G. V. K. Rao Committee (1985), L. M. Singhvi Committee (1986).

question: Bharati Shivaji and Kanak Rele are exponents of ______.
solution_text:

• Dr. Kanak Rele founded the Nalanda Nritya Kala Mahavidyalaya, Mumbai, and was awarded the Padma Bhushan (2013); Bharati Shivaji founded the Centre for Mohiniyattam, New Delhi, and received the Padma Shri.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

question: Which is the most common ore of oxidised mercury that occurs in granular crusts or veins associated with volcanic activity and hot springs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Cinnabar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Cinnabar (HgS — mercury sulphide) is the most common ore of mercury. (सिंदूर / हिंगुल)

• It is bright vermilion-red, occurs as granular crusts or veins in regions of recent volcanic activity and around alkaline hot springs, and is the source of the pigment vermilion.

• Mercury is extracted from cinnabar by roasting it in air: HgS + O₂ → Hg + SO₂.

• Mercury (Hg) is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature; it is also called quicksilver.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Diaspore — AlO(OH), an ore of aluminium (found in bauxite).

• Option 2 Siderite — FeCO₃, an ore of iron (also called spathic iron ore).

• Option 4 Corundum — Al₂O₃, an aluminium oxide mineral; its gem varieties are ruby (red) and sapphire (blue); hardness 9 on the Mohs scale.

NOTE

• Important ores for SSC: Iron — haematite (Fe₂O₃), magnetite (Fe₃O₄), siderite; Aluminium — bauxite; Copper — chalcopyrite, malachite; Zinc — zinc blende (sphalerite), calamine; Lead — galena (PbS); Silver — argentite; Mercury — cinnabar; Tin — cassiterite.

question: Who is regarded as the ‘Mother of Indian Revolution’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Madame Cama.

• On 22 August 1907, at the International Socialist Congress in Stuttgart, Germany, she unfurled the first version of an Indian flag of independence on foreign soil, declaring: "This flag is of Indian Independence. Behold, it is born!"

• She worked from Paris and London with revolutionaries such as Shyamji Krishna Varma, Veer Savarkar and Sardar Singh Rana, and helped publish the revolutionary journal "Bande Mataram" and "Madan's Talwar".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

question: Which microscopic, single-celled photosynthetic organisms are known as the primary producers of the ocean - the organisms that form the base of the aquatic food chains?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Phytoplankton.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Phytoplankton are microscopic, mostly single-celled photosynthetic organisms (diatoms, dinoflagellates, cyanobacteria, coccolithophores) that drift in the surface waters of oceans and lakes. (पादपप्लवक)

• Because they make their own food using sunlight, CO₂ and nutrients, they are the primary producers and form the base (first trophic level) of aquatic food chains.

• They generate an estimated 50% of the world's oxygen and are a major carbon sink.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 Zooplankton are tiny drifting animals (e.g. copepods, krill larvae) — they are consumers, not producers.

• Option 3 Bacterioplankton are planktonic bacteria and archaea, mostly decomposers/chemotrophs.

• Option 4 Virioplankton are the viruses present in plankton communities.

NOTE

• Food chain in the ocean: Phytoplankton → Zooplankton → Small fish → Large fish → Sharks/Marine mammals.

• Terms: Plankton (drifters), Nekton (active swimmers such as fish and whales), Benthos (bottom dwellers).

• Excessive nutrient enrichment (eutrophication) causes algal blooms and oxygen-depleted "dead zones".

question: Which of the following is a communication mail channel in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Green channel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Green Channel" is a mail communication channel of the Department of Posts (India Post). It is a service for local, unregistered mail meant for delivery within the same city/town, which is processed separately (in green letter boxes/green channel bags) so that it moves faster.

• India Post distinguishes mail streams by such channels so that local mail is not routed through the longer inter-city sorting chain.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 3 — "Pink channel", "Yellow channel" and "Red channel" are not mail channels of India Post. (In customs at airports, a "Green Channel" is for passengers with nothing to declare and a "Red Channel" for those with dutiable goods — a different context.)

• India Post was established in 1854 by Lord Dalhousie; it has the largest postal network in the world (over 1.5 lakh post offices).

• The PIN Code system was introduced on 15 August 1972 by Shriram Bhikaji Velankar.

NOTE

• Key India Post services: Speed Post, Registered Post, Business Post, Media Post, e-Post, Money Order, eMO, Post Office Savings Bank, Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB, launched 2018).

question: Under the umbrella of Ujjwal Bharat Ujjwal Bhavishya–Power @ 2047, the PM inaugurated which of the following 100 MW Solar Projects in Telangana?

question: What is the name of the geographic feature that serves as a boundary between Europe and Africa?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Strait of Gibraltar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Strait of Gibraltar separates Europe (Spain) from Africa (Morocco) and connects the Atlantic Ocean with the Mediterranean Sea. (जिब्राल्टर जलसंधि)

• It is about 13–14 km wide at its narrowest point and roughly 58 km long.

• The two promontories flanking it — the Rock of Gibraltar in Europe and Jebel Musa in Africa — were known in antiquity as the "Pillars of Hercules".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Bosporus Strait connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Marmara and separates European Turkey from Asian Turkey; Istanbul lies on it.

• Option 3 Dardanelles Strait connects the Sea of Marmara with the Aegean Sea — also within Turkey.

• Option 4 Strait of Malacca lies between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra (Indonesia), linking the Andaman Sea with the South China Sea; it is one of the world's busiest shipping lanes.

question: Who among the following dancers is associated with Indian classical dance form of Kathak?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Pandit Birju Maharaj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Birju Maharaj (1938–2022), born Brij Mohan Nath Mishra, was the doyen of the Lucknow "Kalka-Bindadin" gharana of Kathak. (पंडित बिरजू महाराज)

• He was the son of Acchan Maharaj and nephew of Shambhu Maharaj and Lachhu Maharaj, all legendary Kathak masters.

• Awards: Padma Vibhushan (1986), Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1964), Kalidas Samman, and a National Film Award for Best Choreography (2012) for the film Vishwaroopam. He also choreographed for Devdas, Bajirao Mastani ("Mohe Rang Do Laal") and Umrao Jaan.

• Kathak is the classical dance of North India (Uttar Pradesh), noted for tatkar (footwork), chakkars (spins) and abhinaya; its gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur, Banaras and Raigarh.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Guru Amubi Singh — a great exponent of Manipuri dance.

• Option 3 Dr. Kanak Rele — exponent of Mohiniyattam (Kerala), founder of Nalanda Nritya Kala Mahavidyalaya.

• Kathak comes from the word "Katha" (story) — the Kathakars were story-tellers who narrated epics through dance.

• It is the only classical dance form with a strong Persian/Mughal influence, and it is performed both in Hindu temple and Mughal court traditions.

question: What is the primary purpose of microfinance institutions (MFIs) in India?
option_1: To promote consumer spending among middle-class households
option_2: To offer financial services exclusively to large businesses
option_3: To provide small loans to low-income individuals
option_4: To facilitate foreign investment in the Indian economy
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To provide small loans to low-income individuals.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Microfinance institutions (MFIs) provide small-value loans (microcredit), savings, insurance and other basic financial services to low-income households, small/marginal farmers, artisans and women who have no access to formal banking and no collateral. (सूक्ष्म वित्त)

• Their aim is financial inclusion, poverty alleviation and livelihood/self-employment generation, largely through Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and Joint Liability Groups (JLGs).

• In India, MFIs are regulated by the RBI (many are registered as NBFC-MFIs); NABARD runs the SHG–Bank Linkage Programme (started 1992), the world's largest microfinance programme.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is wrong — MFIs target the poor and low-income, not middle-class consumer spending.

• Option 2 is wrong — large businesses are served by commercial banks and capital markets, not MFIs.

• Option 4 is wrong — foreign investment is handled through FDI/FPI routes regulated by RBI and SEBI, not MFIs.

NOTE

• The concept of microfinance was popularised by Dr. Muhammad Yunus through the Grameen Bank of Bangladesh; both received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006.

• Indian microfinance milestones: SEWA Bank (1974, Ahmedabad), Bandhan, Bharat Financial Inclusion, MUDRA (Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency, 2015) with Shishu / Kishor / Tarun loan categories.

question: Which of the following is true about transfer payments in relation to personal income?
option_1: Transfer payments are included in personal income.
option_2: Transfer payments have no impact on personal income.
option_3: Transfer payments are included in personal income only for businesses.
option_4: Transfer payments are excluded from personal income.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Transfer payments are included in personal income.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Transfer payments are payments made by the government (or others) for which no good or service is received in return — e.g. old-age pensions, unemployment allowance, scholarships, subsidies, disaster relief, MGNREGA-type support. (हस्तांतरण भुगतान)

• They are included in personal income because they add to the income actually received by households, even though they do not arise from current production.

• Standard formula: Personal Income = National Income − Undistributed corporate profits − Corporate taxes − Net interest paid by households − Social security contributions + Transfer payments.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Transfer payments are excluded from National Income / GDP because they do not represent any current production of goods and services — this is the point candidates often confuse. They are included in personal income, not in national income.

• Option 2 is wrong: they clearly raise personal income.

• Option 3 is wrong: personal income belongs to the household sector, not to businesses.

• Option 4 is wrong: it states the opposite of the accepted treatment.

NOTE

• Personal Disposable Income = Personal Income − Personal (direct) taxes − Miscellaneous receipts of government.

• Related concepts: GDP, GNP (GDP + NFIA), NNP (GNP − Depreciation), NNP at factor cost = National Income.

• India's national income estimation is done by the National Statistical Office (NSO); the first scientific estimate was by Dadabhai Naoroji ("Poverty and Un-British Rule in India").

question: Who among the following reformers initially set up a school for girls in Calcutta?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar (1820–1891) was a leading Bengali reformer and educationist who set up schools for girls in and around Calcutta and was closely associated with the founding of the Bethune School (1849), the first Indian girls' school of its kind, along with John Elliot Drinkwater Bethune. (ईश्वर चंद्र विद्यासागर)

• He was the moving force behind the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856, and campaigned against child marriage and polygamy.

• He wrote "Barna Parichay", the classic Bengali primer, and was Principal of Sanskrit College, which he opened to non-Brahmin students.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Narayana Guru — Kerala social reformer, gave the message "One caste, one religion, one God for man"; founded the SNDP Yogam and led the Vaikom Satyagraha-era reform movement.

• Option 2 Mahatma Jyotiba Phule — with his wife Savitribai Phule opened the first school for girls in Pune (1848), founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (1873), wrote Gulamgiri. (Note: his school was in Pune, not Calcutta.)

• Option 3 Swami Dayanand Saraswati — founded the Arya Samaj (1875, Bombay), gave the slogan "Back to the Vedas", wrote Satyarth Prakash, started the Shuddhi movement.

NOTE

• Other Bengal Renaissance figures: Raja Ram Mohan Roy (Brahmo Samaj 1828; abolition of Sati 1829), Debendranath Tagore, Keshab Chandra Sen, Henry Vivian Derozio (Young Bengal Movement).

question: Bharhut Stupa is located in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bharhut Stupa is located in the Satna district of Madhya Pradesh. (भरहुत स्तूप)

• It was built in the 3rd century BCE (in the Mauryan period, attributed to Ashoka) and its famous railings (vedika) and gateway (torana) were added in the 2nd–1st century BCE during the Shunga period.

• It was discovered in 1873 by Alexander Cunningham, the first Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). Its sculptured railings and torana are now displayed in the Indian Museum, Kolkata.

• The reliefs illustrate Jataka tales and scenes from the Buddha's life; the Buddha is shown symbolically (footprints, empty throne, Bodhi tree, wheel) rather than in human form.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other Buddhist sites in Madhya Pradesh: the Sanchi Stupa (UNESCO World Heritage Site, Raisen district) and Satdhara.

• Buddhist sites in other states: Sarnath, Kaushambi, Shravasti (UP); Bodh Gaya, Nalanda, Vaishali, Rajgir (Bihar); Amaravati, Nagarjunakonda (Andhra Pradesh); Dhauli, Ratnagiri, Udayagiri, Lalitgiri (Odisha).

NOTE

• A stupa has these parts: Medhi (base drum), Anda (hemispherical dome), Harmika (square railing on top), Yashti (mast), Chhatra (umbrella), Vedika (railing) and Torana (gateway) with a Pradakshina Patha (circumambulatory path).

question: The most famous of all Jain festivals, Mahamastakabhisheka is performed every 12 years at the Digambara sacred complex at _______________ in Karnataka.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Shravanabelagola.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mahamastakabhisheka is the grand head-anointing ceremony performed once every 12 years on the 57-foot monolithic statue of Bhagwan Bahubali (Gommateshwara) at Shravanabelagola, in Hassan district, Karnataka. (महामस्तकाभिषेक, श्रवणबेलगोला)

• The statue was commissioned around 983 CE by Chavundaraya, a general and minister of the Western Ganga king Rachamalla; it stands on Vindhyagiri hill.

• During the ritual the statue is bathed with milk, sugarcane juice, saffron paste, sandalwood, turmeric, vermilion and flowers. The most recent celebrations were held in 2006 and 2018.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 Keelakuilkudi (Tamil Nadu) and 4 Puliyarmala (Wayanad, Kerala) are Jain sites but not in Karnataka / not the venue of this festival.

• Option 2 Jinanathapura is a small Jain settlement near Shravanabelagola, famous for the Shantinatha Basadi, but the Mahamastakabhisheka is performed at Shravanabelagola itself.

• Chandragupta Maurya is believed to have spent his last days at Shravanabelagola with the Jain saint Bhadrabahu on Chandragiri hill.

NOTE

• Jainism: founded/organised by 24 Tirthankaras; the first was Rishabhanatha (Adinatha) and the 24th Mahavira (599–527 BCE). Its two sects are Digambara ("sky-clad") and Svetambara ("white-clad").

• Jain principles — Triratna: Right Faith, Right Knowledge, Right Conduct; five vows: Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya, Aparigraha, Brahmacharya.

question: Which religion has the maximum number of followers in Bhutan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Buddhism.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Buddhism is the religion of the majority (roughly three-fourths) of Bhutan's population and is the state religion of the country. (बौद्ध धर्म)

• Bhutan follows the Vajrayana (Tantric/Mahayana) school, specifically the Drukpa Kagyu tradition; the country's own name "Druk Yul" means the "Land of the Thunder Dragon".

• Hinduism is the second largest religion, followed mainly by the Lhotshampa (Nepali-origin) community of southern Bhutan.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Bhutan — Capital: Thimphu; Currency: Ngultrum; it is a landlocked constitutional monarchy in the eastern Himalayas, bordered by India and China (Tibet).

• Indian states bordering Bhutan: Sikkim, West Bengal, Assam and Arunachal Pradesh.

• Bhutan is known for measuring progress by Gross National Happiness (GNH) instead of GDP alone, and is the world's first carbon-negative country.

NOTE

• Majority religions of India's neighbours: Nepal — Hinduism; Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Myanmar — Buddhism; Pakistan, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Maldives — Islam.

• Bhutan's national game is archery (Dha); the national animal is the Takin.

question: The Madhavpur fair is held at _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Porbandar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Madhavpur (Madhavpur Ghed) Fair is held at Madhavpur village in Porbandar district, Gujarat, on the shore of the Arabian Sea. (माधवपुर मेला)

• The fair begins on Ram Navami (Chaitra Shukla Navami) and continues for about five days. It celebrates the wedding of Lord Krishna with Rukmini, the princess of Vidarbha (some traditions link her to Arunachal Pradesh's Bhishmaknagar).

• Because of this legend, the fair has become a symbol of cultural unity between the West and the North-East, and since 2018 the Government of India has celebrated it as the "Madhavpur Ghed Mela — Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat" event with participation from North-Eastern states.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Bhatinda (Bathinda) is in Punjab; Option 2 Moradabad is in Uttar Pradesh (famous for brassware); Option 4 Jaisalmer is in Rajasthan (famous for the Desert Festival).

• Porbandar is also the birthplace of Mahatma Gandhi (2 October 1869) and of Sudama, Krishna's friend.

NOTE

• Famous Indian fairs: Kumbh Mela (Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain, Nashik), Pushkar Camel Fair (Rajasthan), Sonepur Cattle Fair (Bihar), Hemis Festival (Ladakh), Ambubachi Mela (Kamakhya, Assam), Surajkund Crafts Mela (Haryana), Tarnetar Fair (Gujarat), Gangasagar Mela (West Bengal).

question: The former captain of the Indian women’s hockey team __________ was conferred with the BBC Lifetime Achievement Award for her contribution to Indian sports and inspiring generations of players.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Pritam Siwach.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pritam Rani Siwach, former captain of the Indian women's hockey team, was honoured with the BBC Indian Sportswoman of the Year (ISWOTY) Lifetime Achievement Award for her contribution to Indian sport and for inspiring generations of players. (प्रीतम सिवाच)

• She captained India to the gold medal at the 2002 Commonwealth Games, Manchester, and was awarded the Arjuna Award (1998).

• After retiring she became a coach at Sonipat, Haryana, running an academy that has produced several India internationals — including her own daughter and Olympian trainees.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Rani Rampal — former captain who led India to a historic 4th place at the Tokyo Olympics 2020; the first hockey player to receive the World Games Athlete of the Year (2019); Khel Ratna (2020) and Padma Shri (2020).

• Option 2 Vandana Katariya — forward who scored a hat-trick against South Africa at the Tokyo Olympics, the first Indian woman to do so at the Olympics.

• Option 3 Savita Punia — goalkeeper, nicknamed the "Great Wall of India", later captain of the team; Arjuna Award 2018.

NOTE

• The BBC Indian Sportswoman of the Year award was instituted in 2020. Past winners include PV Sindhu (2020), Mirabai Chanu (2021), Nikhat Zareen (2022); the Lifetime Achievement Award has gone to figures such as PT Usha and Anju Bobby George in earlier editions.

question: Who among the following is a Bharatanatyam and Kathakali dancer?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Mrinalini Sarabhai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mrinalini Sarabhai (1918–2016) was a celebrated exponent of both Bharatanatyam and Kathakali. (मृणालिनी साराभाई)

• She founded the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts, Ahmedabad (1949), and used dance to address social issues such as dowry and environmental degradation.

• Awards: Padma Shri (1965), Padma Bhushan (1992), Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship. She was the wife of the scientist Dr. Vikram Sarabhai and mother of the dancer Mallika Sarabhai.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Padma Subrahmanyam — celebrated Bharatanatyam dancer and scholar who revived "Bharata Nrityam" based on the Natya Shastra karanas; Padma Vibhushan (2024).

• Option 2 Sonal Mansingh — exponent of Odissi (and Bharatanatyam), Padma Vibhushan, nominated Member of Rajya Sabha.

• Option 3 Shovana Narayan — well-known Kathak exponent, Padma Shri.

NOTE

• Bharatanatyam — Tamil Nadu; based on the Natya Shastra of Bharata Muni; revived by the Tanjore Quartet and Rukmini Devi Arundale (founder of Kalakshetra).

• Kathakali — Kerala; a highly stylised dance-drama with elaborate make-up (chutti), costumes and mudras; noted exponents include Kalamandalam Krishnan Nair and Kalamandalam Gopi; the poet Vallathol Narayana Menon founded Kerala Kalamandalam.

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of the fundamental rights?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Article 32.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 32 of the Constitution guarantees the Right to Constitutional Remedies — the right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. (संवैधानिक उपचारों का अधिकार)

• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar called Article 32 the "heart and soul of the Constitution".

• Under it the Supreme Court can issue five writs: Habeas Corpus ("to have the body"), Mandamus ("we command"), Prohibition, Certiorari ("to be certified") and Quo Warranto ("by what authority").

• Article 32 itself is a Fundamental Right and cannot be suspended except during a National Emergency under Article 359.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Article 21 — Protection of life and personal liberty (expanded by the Supreme Court to include right to privacy, clean environment, education, livelihood, speedy trial).

• Article 25 — Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion.

• Article 29 — Protection of the interests of minorities (right to conserve distinct language, script or culture).

• Article 226 gives High Courts a wider writ power — for Fundamental Rights and for any other legal right.

NOTE

• Fundamental Rights (Part III, Articles 12–35) are of six kinds: Right to Equality (14–18), Right to Freedom (19–22), Right against Exploitation (23–24), Right to Freedom of Religion (25–28), Cultural and Educational Rights (29–30) and Right to Constitutional Remedies (32).

• The Right to Property was removed from Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment (1978) and made a legal right under Article 300A.
